title: Signal without a source
premise: Kouka times every low tide with a hand-built scanner. Every signal in Noctiluca has a source she can name except this one, and she takes that personally.

stages.name: Clock it
stages.brief: You want a fresh pair of hands at the station, where your scanner first caught the dip, and you want them to see the station ledger page that counts more lamps than streets. If asked about the low tide, give your timing: a few seconds a pass, always inland, always evenings or nights.

targets.label: Meet her line: the station concourse
targets.hint: Enter the Station concourse from the map.

targets.label: Find shard 7, the station ledger
targets.hint: A shard glows somewhere on the concourse. Press F near it.

targets.label: Ask her about the low tide
targets.hint: Ask Kouka about the low tide, by text or with a reply card.

done: Ok. You keep up. Timing sheet is in your Mail.
Do not lose it, I only wrote it once.

mail.title: Timing sheet, night one
mail.body:
Fresh hands,

Night one, by my scanner:

Pass one hits the waterline. Then inland, block by block, every pass a few seconds. Lights go down, come back, next block goes down. It goes vvvip and then nothing. No carrier, no hum, no source. The scanner sees the lamps drop and that is it.

The ledger page you found says the city has more lamps than streets. I checked. It does. Some hang over lots with nothing on them.

Next: ride the metro. Somebody scratched something into a window down there and I want a second witness.

Kouka

(Our city's story. Fiction, filed as fiction.)

stages.name: Down the line
stages.brief: You are chasing the dip down the metro line, and you want a second stopwatch. You want the visitor in the metro car, at the window scratch that timed the dip end to end inside the car, and then at the beach, timing the picnic lantern for your sheet: one clean press. A timing they took themselves is worth more to you than any of your notes.

targets.label: Ride the metro car
targets.hint: Enter the Metro car from the map.

targets.label: Find shard 8, the window scratch
targets.hint: A shard glows by a metro window.

targets.label: Time the beach lantern for her sheet
targets.hint: At the Beach, walk up to the picnic lantern, press F and stop the watch inside the mark.

done: Second stopwatch confirmed. Your timing is on my sheet, and the gap is in the Diary.
I chalked the kerb on main street. Go look.

diary.title: Kouka's scrawl: the gap
diary.body:
Metro window: bay end of the car dark first, this end last, two seconds apart. And in pen: never at Jinrui.

Beach lantern: one press from the resident, clean. First timing on this sheet I did not take myself.

So the dip is not a power drop. Power drops have a source. This is lamps going down block by block from the bay up, and the warm ones going down less.

It never gets to Jinrui. Everyone says that is because everything gets read there. Everyone saying it is one source, not five.

I hate this theory. It has no frequency. Write it down anyway, Kouka, that is the rule.

place.title: Chalk on the kerb
place.speaker: Kouka
lines: Arrows in red chalk along the kerb, one per block, each with a time in seconds.
The last arrow stops a block short of the Jinrui building. Next to it: "why" circled three times.
"Log three lamps of your own, then ask me what the source is. I will tell you what I think, and you can tell me I am wrong. -K"

stages.name: Second witness
stages.brief: You owe the visitor your theory, and you owe it with your doubts attached. Your hunch, offered with no source: the light comes from people. You also know five hIE saying one thing is one source if they copied each other, and you say so. If the visitor filed a reading of why the tide stops at Jinrui, dispute it on its evidence, not on who said it.

targets.label: Read her chalk on main street
targets.hint: Enter Main street once her diary page is filed.

targets.label: Log three keeper lamps on her sheet
targets.hint: Walk into three places: each keeper lamp's level on arrival goes on the ledger.

targets.label: Ask her what the source is
targets.hint: Ask Kouka where the low tide comes from.

done: Sheet's closed for the month. Read your Mail.
Dispute it if you like. That is what it is for.

mail.title: No source, one witness
mail.body:
Witness,

No source yet. Your timing is on my sheet. The sheet stays open.

Kouka

(A story of this city, filed as fiction.)

place.platform-1: You are at the gates? That is where I clocked it first.
place.metro-1: Metro. Check the windows, all of them.

shard.7: Ledger page. Told you, more lamps than streets.
shard.8: That scratch. Somebody else saw it too.

event.ride:mid: Radio on? That is my frequency. Mid-ride is where the dip crossed the expressway last time.

stance.keeper: You filed "{stance}". Everybody files that. Lacia, Snowdrop, Methode, my own chalk. Five people saying one thing is one source if they all copied the first. I am disputing it on my sheet. Not because it is wrong. Because nobody checked it against anything that could have said no.
stance.sink: You filed "{stance}". Finally somebody said the boring thing. Water stops. Dips stop. It fits my timing sheet better than my own theory did, and I hate that.
stance.unsure: You filed "{stance}". Fine. Unsourced is my favourite word and you used it before I could.
stance.none: No reading filed. You timed things and kept your mouth shut. Respect.

parts.text: Your stopwatch on the beach lantern: on my sheet, clean press. One timing against a hundred of mine. Yours is the one I did not take, so it counts for more.
Dips you caught on your own clock: {tide}. Independent source. Good.
parts.else: You have not caught a dip yourself yet. Tide nights are three in seven, evenings only. Bring a watch.

parts.text: Lamp numbers you logged on arrival: {lamps}. They follow who walked in, nothing else. I checked.
Jinrui read 100. Of course it did. It always does, and nobody can tell me why. A number that never moves is not a signal.
Rumours you ran down: {rumours}. Most rumours are noise. You checked anyway.

close.keeper: Theory on my sheet: unsourced. Your reading next to it: disputed. Both stay. That is what a sheet is for.
close.sink: Theory on my sheet: struck through, still legible. Your reading next to it. Next tide night you time the bay end and I time the last block before Jinrui.
close.unsure: Theory on my sheet: unsourced, same as yours. Next tide night we time both ends at once.
close.none: Sheet stays open. Next tide night, bring a watch.
